text.title: Go HTTP Handlers (Gin / Echo / Chi / stdlib) Core Rules
text.summary: 14 testable rules every Go HTTP Handlers (Gin / Echo / Chi / stdlib) application MUST enforce. HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override them. Router configuration patterns for Gin and Echo, including correct middleware order and subrouter/group patterns. Covers the stdlib 1.22 enhanced muxer as a zero-dependency alternative. Handlers as methods on a dependency-injecting struct, with request DTOs using binding/validate tags, typed response structs, and RFC 7807 error mapping instead of raw err.Error() in JSON. Rules preventing the most common Go HTTP handler mistakes: mixed framework signatures, raw err.Error() in responses, missing server timeouts, and test generation gaps.

rule.statement: ONE framework per service; mixed routers across files are FORBIDDEN. Lock the router choice (Gin, Echo, Chi, stdlib) in the system prompt for any LLM session. Reject any file where Gin and Echo imports coexist. Add a CI lint check for the unwanted import.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal Go reviews. LLMs mix handler signatures when context windows overflow. func(c *gin.Context) and func(c echo.Context) error are incompatible; mixed files produce confusing compile errors. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Handlers MUST be methods on a struct holding dependencies (services, loggers), never package-level funcs with globals. Define handlers as methods on a struct that holds service dependencies (logger, services). Never use package-level globals (var DB *sql.DB) inside handlers. Inject dependencies at construction time.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Hexagonal architecture. Package-level globals prevent parallel test execution (shared state between test cases) and make dependency substitution impossible without init() hacks. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Request DTOs MUST carry binding/validate tags; controller binds + validates before calling service.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: go-playground/validator docs. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Responses MUST be typed structs (never `map[string]any` from a handler).
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Internal reviews. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Errors MUST be returned to middleware (`c.Error(err)`) that renders RFC 7807; handlers never write JSON for errors.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: error-handling methodology. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Tests MUST be table-driven over `httptest` with the actual router; mock the service interface. Test handlers with httptest.NewRecorder + router.ServeHTTP. Cover both happy-path and unhappy-path (missing required field, invalid type, oversized body). Do not spin a real server for unit tests.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Effective Go testing. httptest tests run in parallel, start instantly, and exercise the full middleware chain. Agents generating only happy-path tests miss the most common field-validation regressions. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Handlers MUST pass `r.Context()` / `c.Request.Context()` to service calls; never `context.Background()`. `context.Background()` belongs to `main()` and test setup only. Pass r.Context() (or c.Request.Context() in Gin) as the first argument into every service call. Never use context.Background() inside a handler.
rule.rationale: Rule rooted in source: Go context docs. `Background()` detaches from the request, so cancellation never propagates and a long downstream call keeps burning resources after the client has gone. context.Background() ignores client disconnection. Long-running service calls (DB, HTTP) continue consuming resources after the client has gone away. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Use `gin.New()` / `echo.New()` and register every middleware explicitly. `gin.Default()` is FORBIDDEN.
rule.rationale: `gin.Default()` bundles its own Logger + Recovery with opinionated formats; teams then add their own and end up running two Recoverys and logging in a format that carries no trace id. Explicit composition is the only way the order in r-middleware-order is auditable. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Do NOT spawn a goroutine inside a handler that captures `c` or uses `c.Request.Context()` after the handler returns. For genuine background work derive `context.WithoutCancel(c.Request.Context())` plus an explicit timeout, and pass extracted values by argument.
rule.rationale: The request context is cancelled the moment the handler returns, so the background goroutine dies with `context canceled`; and `gin.Context` itself is request-scoped and not thread-safe, so the race detector flags it. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: A handler does exactly four things: bind request → validate via binding tags → call ONE service method → translate to HTTP. No business logic, and under 40 lines.
rule.rationale: A thin handler is testable as a transport adapter; logic inside one can only be exercised by standing up the whole HTTP stack. The 40-line bound is what makes the rule greppable rather than aspirational. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: `http.Server` MUST set all four timeouts explicitly — `ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout`. Never leave the zero defaults. Reasonable starting values: 5s / 30s / 30s / 120s.
rule.rationale: Zero means unbounded: a client that never finishes sending headers holds a goroutine and a file descriptor forever (Slowloris), and `r.Run(":8080")` configures none of them. Set ReadHeaderTimeout, WriteTimeout, and IdleTimeout on http.Server. Frameworks do not set these; a server without timeouts is vulnerable to slowloris attacks and resource exhaustion. A client that never finishes sending headers holds a goroutine and file descriptor indefinitely. ReadHeaderTimeout terminates such connections. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: Register middleware in this order: Recovery (outermost), RequestID, Logger, Auth (on protected groups). Recovery must be outermost so panics are caught before the logger middleware runs. Logger must be after RequestID so the request ID is available in logs.
rule.rationale: Recovery placed inside Logger means a panicking handler crashes the Logger middleware before it can write the log line. The recovery response is then written by a dead middleware, producing a garbled or empty body. Violations trigger the matching antipattern in 03-failure-modes.xml.

rule.statement: For new services without a team-wide framework standard, prefer the stdlib 1.22 muxer (http.NewServeMux with METHOD /path patterns) over adding a framework dependency. Add a framework only when its features (validator, response helpers) justify the dependency.
rule.rationale: The 1.22 muxer supports method-specific routing (GET /users/{id}) and path parameters (r.PathValue) natively, eliminating the primary reason to reach for Gin/Echo in simple CRUD APIs.

rule.statement: Use c.ShouldBindJSON (not c.Bind) on Gin. ShouldBind returns an error without writing a response; c.Bind writes a 400 directly and the handler continues — producing a double-write bug.
rule.rationale: c.Bind's auto-response behavior is a Gin anti-pattern; handlers that check err after c.Bind may still execute, producing conflicting response writes.

section.title: Conclusion targets used by the decision tree

rule.statement: Run the full procedure; emit an artefact passing the output contract.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions hold and no duplicate exists.

rule.statement: Skip; surface the missing precondition; do not synthesize.
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when preconditions fail.

rule.statement: Update the existing artefact in place (bump version, refresh last_reviewed).
rule.rationale: Terminal target used by 06-decision-tree when a duplicate is found.
